subject: Capacity check: ZenithAI final sizing & temporary hold request
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity check: ZenithAI final sizing & temporary hold request

Team —

ZenithAI (Alex Grover) just moved to legal and procurement but we need to lock a small slice of Dedicated capacity for their POC to guarantee latency in production. They expect to ramp quickly if the pilot metrics look good. Key ask: can we provision a short-term hold (2–4 weeks) on a conservative GPU block while we finalize SLA/contract?

Quick context: Zenith wants to run a multimodal retrieval + generator workload for search + assistant. They estimate sustained 40 qps peak (payloads average 1.5k tokens) with bursts to 90 qps. They prefer a 4xA100 logical capacity, but are open to quantized options if we can show comparable latency.

Immediate questions for Capacity:
- Is there available headroom for a provisional 4xA100 equivalent hold starting late March?
- If not, what is the minimal equivalent we can hold that meets 95th latency SLO (~120ms for generation tails) for 1.5k tokens?
- Any recommendations on batching / KV caching profiles we should propose to Zenith to lower unit cost while meeting latency?

I attached the latest sizing notes from the customer. I need a one-paragraph summary and a recommendation by EOD so I can include it in the procurement packet.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0137
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-03-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity check: ZenithAI final sizing & temporary hold request

Lauren —

Short answer: we have limited flexibility in late March; several reserved pools are in-flight. That said, we can place a provisional hold on an allocation equivalent to ~2xA100 immediately for a 2-week window and extend to 3x for another 2 weeks if we get confirmation next week.

Notes / rationale:
- 4x sustained at 1.5k token tails with 95th ~120ms requires a mix of A100-equivalent plus optimized kernel selection; our runtime sees cost blowup with 90 qps bursts unless KV prefix caching is enforced.
- If the customer adopts a hybrid quantized MPT variant (INT8 / q4f16 profile), we can achieve similar latency with ~2.5x nominal capacity versus 4x full fp32.
- Suggested tactical hold:
  1) Place immediate provisional hold: 2xA100-equivalent (2 weeks)
  2) Conditional extension: escalate to +1x for weeks 3–4 if procurement signs a provisional commitment (email/DocuSign).

I'll attach a short capacity note and the rough perf numbers you can paste into procurement.

Marcus

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-14T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity check: ZenithAI final sizing & temporary hold request

Adding perf validation data —

We ran a matching workload on q4f16 MPT-350B variant (proxy of their model) last week:
- Sustained 40 qps, 1.5k tokens: 95th gen tail = ~140ms on 2xA100-equivalent with aggressive KV caching.
- Burst to 90 qps causes tail to spike to ~320ms unless we:
  * Enable request-level throttling OR
  * Route bursts to a warm fallback pool with slightly higher cost but lower tail variance.

Recommendation: for the POC, we can recommend a provisional config: 2xA100-equivalent hold + routing policy that gates bursts to a separate 1x warm pool (auto-burst enabled). That keeps the customer within latency SLO for normal traffic and avoids over-committing core capacity for infrequent spikes.

I also drafted a one-paragraph blurb you can paste into procurement. See below.

— blurb —
Redwood recommends a provisional 2xA100-equivalent Dedicated hold for an initial 2-week pilot window with a conditional +1x extension based on committed execution. We propose routing burst traffic (above 50 qps) to a warm standby pool to preserve 95th percentile latency for production-like loads. A quantized model profile (q4f16) is suggested to reduce unit GPU needs while maintaining acceptable generation latency.

Priyom
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren / team —

This is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side before we move procurement: 
- Our POC timeline is tight: pilot runs Apr 1–Apr 21. We need the provisional hold to start Mar 28 to run staging and validation.
- SLA question: if we take the proposed routing profile, can you commit to the 95th latency target (120–150ms) for production traffic (40 qps sustained)? We understand bursts may be routed to a warm fallback, but we need an SLA carve-out for the pilot that guarantees the core hold will meet the stated SLOs.
- DocuSign: procurement wants a provisional agreement they can sign that specifies hold terms, extension triggers, and cancellation notice.

We can sign a provisional commitment to secure the hold if you send the DocuSign link + short summary.

—Alex

Alex —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We can do the provisional hold per Marcus/Priyom's recommendation: 2xA100-equivalent reserved from 2028-03-28 for an initial 2-week window with a conditional +1x extension for weeks 3–4 on confirmation.

SLA: for the reserved core pool we will commit to a 95th percentile generation tail of <=150ms for the stated test profile (40 qps sustained, 1.5k avg tokens) when using the recommended quantized model profile and KV caching. The pilot DocuSign will include a carve-out that routes bursts above 50 qps to a warm fallback pool (no 95th latency guarantee for those routed bursts), and it will specify extension triggers and cancellation notice (48 hours).

I attached the provisional agreement draft and the capacity plan for your legal/procurement review. If procurement can sign the DocuSign by EOD 2028-03-20 we will hold the provisional capacity as discussed.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/rooms/zenithai-zen-4592
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9876543210

Next step: procurement signs provisional, Marcus files the hold, Priyom will coordinate test plan with your infra.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into staging for you.

Lauren
